reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch G2-NA-Q2-Harden (mat_g2_na_q2_4), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Every sample item directly fulfills the requirement of subtracting numbers where both numbers are less than 100 with regrouping. The sample set exercises 2-digit minus 1-digit subtraction with regrouping (e.g., "What is 30 − 3?", "60 − 2 = ___") and 2-digit minus 2-digit subtraction with regrouping across decade boundaries and arbitrary 2-digit values (e.g., "What is 93 − 65?", "60 − 51 = ___", "20 − 15 = ___"). In all instances, the units digit of the minuend is smaller than the units digit of the subtrahend, necessitating regrouping.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The sample set provides balanced and comprehensive coverage across the full scope of the competency. Both specified sub-cases are thoroughly tested: 2-digit minus 1-digit numbers (such as "What is 20 − 1?" and "90 − 2 = 92. True or False?") and 2-digit minus 2-digit numbers (such as "What is 93 − 65?", "What is 60 − 46?", and "80 − 78 = 2. True or False?"). In addition, multiple problem structures are covered including direct computation, cloze equation completion, part-whole relationships, and word contexts.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: All items are developmentally appropriate for Grade 2 Quarter 2 learners. The linguistic complexity is appropriately constrained, using clear and familiar vocabulary (e.g., "What is 30 − 3?", "The total is 90 and one part is 18. What is the other part?", "There are 30 baskets on the table. Moses takes away 28 baskets. How many baskets are left on the table? The answer is 2. True or False?"). Distractors target common place-value errors (e.g., adding instead of subtracting or subtracting without regrouping) without inducing extraneous cognitive load.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The sample exhibits an excellent variety of item variants and pedagogical formatters. These include standard multiple-choice arithmetic ("What is 93 − 65?"), cloze equation completion ("60 − 51 = ___", "30 − 21 = ___"), number-line / backward counting ("The dot is at 50 and it moves backward 1 number. Starting from 50, just count back 1 number. Which number will the dot land on?"), part-whole missing addend ("The total is 30 and one part is 23. What is the other part?"), error detection ("Dante solved: "30 − 14 = ___". Dante says the missing number is 16. Is Dante correct?"), and True/False assertions ("80 − 78 = 2. True or False?").

competency_alignment.rationale: All questions strictly align with the MATATAG learning competency without underreaching or exceeding curriculum boundaries. There are no operations beyond subtraction, no 3-digit operands, and no unregrouped calculations. Items like "What is 93 − 65?" and "What is 20 − 12?" stay squarely on 2-digit subtraction with regrouping for numbers under 100.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Numerical bounds strictly adhere to the competency constraint that 'both numbers are less than 100'. Minuends range from 20 to 93 (e.g., 20 in "What is 20 − 1?", 60 in "60 − 51 = ___", 93 in "What is 93 − 65?") and subtrahends range from 1 to 78 (e.g., 1 in "What is 20 − 1?", 78 in "80 − 78 = 2. True or False?"). All resulting differences remain positive whole numbers within the grade-appropriate range.
